name: stri_trim_left
title: Trim Characters from the Left and/or Right Side of a String

origin.description: Drop a leading run of code points that are not preserved.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to trim.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Class of code points to preserve, unless negate is TRUE.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, complement the pattern before trimming.

origin.details: pattern names the code points to preserve when negate is FALSE, and the code points to trim when negate is TRUE. The default \P{Wspace} preserves every non-whitespace code point, so whitespace is trimmed. \p{Z} does not include tab. Trimming removes only a leading or trailing run; characters between the first and last preserved code point stay. stri_trim, stri_trim_both, stri_trim_left, and stri_trim_right are separate functions.
origin.example:
x <- stri_trim_left("   aaa")
sentence <- paste0('stri_trim_left("   aaa") returns ', x, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Drop a leading run of code points that are not preserved.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Class of code points to preserve, unless negate is true.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, complement the pattern before trimming.

translation.details: pattern names the code points to preserve when negate is false, and the code points to trim when negate is true. The default \P{Wspace} preserves every non-whitespace code point, so whitespace is trimmed. \p{Z} does not include tab. Trimming removes only a leading or trailing run; characters between the first and last preserved code point stay. stri_trim, stri_trim_both, stri_trim_left, and stri_trim_right are separate functions.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_trim_left
x = stri_trim_left("   aaa")
sentence = f'stri_trim_left("   aaa") returns {x[0]}.'
print(sentence)
